item.title: ICLC 2027: International Conference on Live Coding, Call for Participation (Dialogues)
item.description:
Organisation: Lambdasonic (TOPLAP Belgium), Royal Conservatoire of Antwerp and De Singel

Location: Royal Conservatoire of Antwerp and De Singel International Arts Center, Antwerp, Belgium. Open to anyone engaged with live coding; remote participation considered.

Award: NO submission fee. The call does not state artist fees, travel support or accommodation for accepted contributors, so budget for self-funded attendance unless the organisers announce otherwise. Proceedings are published with a DOI per article. Satellite-event hosts can request a Letter of Intent to support their own local funding applications.

Duration: Five-day conference, 9 to 13 March 2027. Workshops are 2 hours (short) or 4 hours (long).

Deadline: 01 Sep 2026

The International Conference on Live Coding is dedicated to practices and research focused on technologies and philosophies that interpret the use of computer code and the public writing of algorithms as performative gestures. The 10th edition runs 9 to 13 March 2027 in Antwerp, hosted by Lambdasonic (TOPLAP Belgium) with the Royal Conservatoire of Antwerp and De Singel. THEME: 'Dialogues', framing live coding as continuous improvisational exchange between coder, machine and audience, and across disciplines. Suggested topics include dialogues between live coding and acoustic musicians, dancers, theatre, classically trained musicians reading live-coded (or graphical) scores, band and jazz-combo settings, live-coder ensembles, ten-minute live-coded mini-operas, DMX lighting systems, graphics and shader live coding, robotics (pen plotters, textile-weaving robots), design-as-performance, community building, diversity/equity/inclusion, accessibility of live coding languages and interfaces, education, and algorave. The venues will facilitate collaborations with resident dancers, a jazz combo (back-line provided: drums, guitar amp, bass amp, piano), a string quartet reading scores a prima vista, visual artists, students and researchers where possible. FORMATS: short papers (2-4 pages) and long papers (5-12 pages) using the provided template; live performances (800-word abstract, max 150-word programme note, technical rider); workshops (short 2h or long 4h, max 700-word abstract, held in English or Dutch); installations (max 700-word abstract, technical questionnaire plus a measured plan or sketch, with the interactive aspect clearly defined); and satellite events. All contributors submit a max 150-word biography. Peer review is single-blind with at least two reviewers per submission. LANGUAGE: submissions must be in English, except that live performance, installation and workshop proposals may also be submitted in another language (workshops: English, Dutch or French) with a machine-translated English version, stated as such. Substantial use of generative AI in writing papers and performance abstracts must be disclosed; proofreading and translation are exempt. In-person presentation is encouraged, with remote proposals considered and sessions live-streamed where possible; the organisers ask attendees to minimise travel impact and to link up with nearby satellite events to turn a long trip into a mini-tour. The call notes attention to access needs, care responsibilities and other barriers to participation. SATELLITE EVENTS: live coding nodes, art schools and other organisations worldwide are invited to host their own events before or after ICLC 2027; submit a declaration of interest via Fourwaves before 1 February 2027 with a principal contact, city and any confirmed details, and join #iclc-satellite-events on the TOPLAP Discord. Hosts are asked to seek local funding for accommodation, travel and artist fees; the committee cannot fund or organise these but will coordinate dates and publish your event. TO APPLY: submit via Fourwaves at https://event.fourwaves.com/iclc2027/pages using the templates at https://codeberg.org/iclc/iclc-templates (read the README for full proposal instructions). Submission deadline extended to 1 September 2026; acceptance notification 1 November 2026. CALL FOR REVIEWERS: anyone active in a live-coding-related field can volunteer by emailing a short description and keywords of their expertise to iclc@lambdasonic.be, the same address for general questions.

item.title: Surel's Place: Month-Long Artist Residency (September 2026 deadline)
item.description:
Organisation: Surel's Place

Location: In person in Garden City, Idaho, USA (Boise area). Residents must live at the home and studio; no studio-only residencies.

Award: Free rent, utilities and wi-fi, a living stipend of USD 100 per week, a USD 300 travel stipend, use of well-maintained bicycles, free or discounted tickets to art events and movies, marketing through Surel's Place channels, and event hosting including logistics and installation help. Each resident also gets a local host to orient them and host their public events. No application fee. NOTE: Surel's Place takes a commission on sales arising from the residency, 35% of retail price on artwork, 45% on ticketed events that are offsite or need contracted services (calculated after administrative expenses), and 15% on books, CDs or other merchandise tangential to the artist's medium. A surcharge may apply to cover additional utility costs if a partner joins.

Duration: One month (longer may be possible if justified in the application). The 1 September deadline covers residencies in January to May of the following year, beginning four months after the deadline; the 1 March deadline covers July to November of the same year.

Deadline: 01 Sep 2026

Surel's Place is a residency in Garden City, Idaho with a two-fold mission: to give artists the time, shelter and professional support their work deserves, and to give the public accessible art experiences including performances, readings, exhibits and workshops. In exchange for the residency, artists offer art experiences back to the community. OPEN TO professional visual, literary and performance artists: painters, writers, musicians, architects, filmmakers, choreographers, any artist who needs a place to focus. LIMITS: because of the property's constraints and proximity to neighbours, it cannot accommodate loud or very messy processes such as welding or blacksmithing. The organisers also note that predominantly conceptual work, work that must be explained to attract a viewer, may not be met with as much enthusiasm by the jurors, and that they welcome artists who want to connect with an audience. Each cycle, one of the five residencies includes outreach to local schools through the PARTNER Schools Program. REQUIREMENTS: maintain residence at the home and studio (no studio-use-only residencies); use the residency in a focused way towards a stated goal with no other employment or work happening simultaneously; visual artists give a show of and/or lecture about their residency work, writers give a reading and discussion session; all artists offer at least one public workshop (2 to 3 hours, minimal lecturing); visual artists donate one piece of art to Surel's Place for future fundraising; writers allow Surel's Place to publish a free-standing excerpt of their residency work in books, broadsides, posters or similar. SALES COMMISSION applies as set out in the funding notes. HOUSE RULES: the non-smoking requirement is non-negotiable and any evidence of smoking is grounds for early termination. Partners are welcome but children and pets cannot be accommodated, no more than two adults may live there during a residency, and partners wanting concurrent residencies must apply and be accepted separately. ELIGIBILITY: applicants must be 25 or older and non-smokers. APPLY by email to info@surelsplace.org with the online Artist in Residence application plus, for VISUAL ARTISTS, a cover letter introducing yourself and saying why you want to be at Surel's Place specifically, a proposal including a workshop outline, a CV, electronic images of 4 to 6 pieces of work and an image list (title, size, medium, year); for LITERARY applicants, cover letter, proposal with workshop outline, CV and PDF work samples with your name and page number in the top right corner (fiction, prose or script no more than 10 typed double-spaced pages; poetry no more than six poems and no more than 10 pages); for OTHER MEDIUMS, cover letter, proposal with workshop outline, CV and electronic samples (contact Surel's Place to discuss sample requirements for your medium). Applications are reviewed by juries of accomplished artists, writers and fine arts professionals, and all applicants are notified by email.

item.title: ESWA Digital Rights Gathering 2026: The (W)horrors Edition (Barcelona)
item.description:
Organisation: European Sex Workers' Rights Alliance (ESWA)

Location: Barcelona, Spain. Gathering runs 2-5 November 2026 (travel day out 1 November, travel day home 5 November).

Award: PARTICIPANTS: fully funded, with travel, accommodation and food covered for all selected participants. SESSION FACILITATORS: EUR 300 per 90-minute session, plus travel, accommodation and meals covered. Free to apply.

Duration: Three days of sessions, 2-4 November 2026, within a 1-5 November travel window

Deadline: Rolling / undated

NO PUBLISHED CLOSING DATE: the call gives no application deadline, so the operative cutoff is the gathering itself on 2-5 November 2026; apply early. The European Sex Workers' Rights Alliance (ESWA) brings back its Digital Rights Gathering in 2026 as The (W)horrors Edition, in Barcelona just after Halloween. It is a capacity and community-building space by and for sex workers, convened to confront the surveillance, censorship and digital violence they face online and to imagine and build more resilient digital futures. A limited number of spaces is reserved for allies working in adjacent digital rights and harm reduction spaces to host sessions. TWO CALLS ARE OPEN. (1) CALL FOR PARTICIPANTS, for sex workers who want to deepen their knowledge of digital rights, online safety and community resilience. Requirements: be a current or former sex worker who is also a member of an organisation in ESWA's network; be available for three days of interactive sessions, skill-sharing and collective learning on 2, 3 and 4 November, and free from 1 November (travel out) through 5 November (travel home), even though some final-day sessions are optional. Selected participants receive full funding covering travel, accommodation and food. (2) CALL FOR TRAINERS AND SESSION PROPOSALS, for facilitators, trainers and educators experienced in digital rights, online safety or sex worker-led organising, who want to deliver an interactive workshop, skill-share or creative session. Sessions run 90 minutes and are compensated at EUR 300 per session, with travel, accommodation and meals covered. Open to current or former sex workers, and to allies with experience in digital rights, digital discrimination, digital security and related fields. SESSION STRANDS: Digital (W)horrors, naming the threats faced online and unpacking how surveillance, censorship and platform policy work against sex workers, including shadowbanning and algorithmic censorship, over-zealous content moderation, law enforcement and third-party surveillance, deplatforming, non-consensual data scraping and retention, and the platforms and policies that enable them; Building Resilience, practical hands-on skills covering open source and privacy-respecting software, how and why to divest from Big Tech platforms, alternative and encrypted communication tools, digital security basics such as protecting data, devices and identity, and other harm-reduction strategies for working and organising online; Imagining Better Futures, creative forward-looking sessions on what a sex worker friendly internet would look like, including prototyping inclusive digital tools, platforms and spaces built by and for sex workers, new apps, alternative social platforms, community-owned tech, and speculative design exercises; Resourcing the Group, sessions focused on care and resilience, including writing and reflection, grounding and somatic exercises, tools for self-care and sustainability in activism, and space for radical rest. The organisers welcome grounded, political and creative contributions from anyone who would like to lead a session. Separate application forms for participants and for session proposals are linked from the call page. Questions: ana@eswalliance.org.

item.title: LATITUDE Artist in Residence 2027 (Chicago)
item.description:
Organisation: LATITUDE Chicago

Location: Chicago, Illinois, USA. No housing stipend offered.

Award: One-month production residency for 8-10 artists: a $1,000 printing stipend, unlimited scanning, a personal studio with a calibrated workstation, staff training and guidance on tech, an organised public event, and lifetime free lab access. No housing stipend. Free to apply before 16 August 2026; a $20 donation thereafter.

Duration: One month (residency takes place in 2027)

Deadline: 01 Sep 2026

The LATITUDE Artist in Residence program (started in 2013) is a one-month production residency where 8-10 artists are granted full access to LATITUDE's facilities and community to develop their practice. Its focus is supporting artists who want to use LATITUDE's printing and scanning services to expand their practice, regardless of medium or experience; past residents include photographers, painters, performance artists, new media artists, and sculptors. WHAT RESIDENTS RECEIVE: a $1,000 printing stipend, unlimited scanning, a personal studio with a calibrated workstation and 24/7 access, training and guidance on tech from staff, an organised public event to present new work, and lifetime free lab access. LATITUDE does not offer a housing stipend but will help schedule studio visits during the month. PUBLIC PROGRAMMING: during the residency each artist puts on one community programming event (past examples include panel discussions, artist talks, performances, workshops, and critiques; a gallery space is available for curation) and is asked to act as a mentor to the community, sharing insights and creative methods. WHO SHOULD APPLY: artists interested in production, education, and tech experimentation; no prior printing experience, art education, or media specificity is required, though professionalism and communication are expected. 2027 PANEL COMMITTEE: Yechen Zhao, B. Ingrid Olson, Teri Carson. TIMELINE: applications open 1 August 2026 (free before 16 August, a $20 donation thereafter) and close 1 September 2026 at 12pm (noon) CST; the selection committee reviews in September, meets to decide finalists in October, and acceptances are sent early November 2026. Apply at latitudechicago.org/artist-in-residence.

item.title: Augur: Researcher (Contractor, remote, part-time)
item.description:
Organisation: Augur

Location: Remote, part-time. The Ashby posting lists the location as United States; the newsletter listing that circulated this role says remote in the US or the UK, so confirm with Augur if you are UK-based.

Award: USD 50 per hour for 8 to 16 hours per week, with scope for expanded hours and responsibility for strong contributors. Initial 3-month contract with opportunity for renewal. Contractor, so no benefits. No application fee.

Duration: Part-time contract, 8 to 16 hours per week, initial 3 months with room to grow

Deadline: Rolling / undated

A part-time remote contractor research role mapping the supply chains behind frontier AI and writing strategic proposals for government and industry decision-makers. RESPONSIBILITIES: map segments of frontier AI and adjacent technology supply chains, with possible focus on specific country ecosystems or on actors across segments such as capital allocation, raw materials, mineral processing, chip design, fabrication, advanced packaging, datasets, datacentres and frontier labs; analyse how ownership stakes, trade relationships and control are likely to evolve under different technological, commercial and geopolitical scenarios; and develop strategic proposals for stakeholders across government and industry. QUALIFICATIONS: strong research and analytical skills with familiarity in one or more of semiconductors, compute infrastructure, capital markets, critical minerals, trade policy or AI governance; clear concise writing for senior policymaker or business-executive audiences; sound strategic judgment and comfort with ambiguity and evolving scope. The posting explicitly asks for people 'adept at using AI models and tools as part of research process' who know when to use them to augment critical thinking and strategic taste rather than replace it. Self-direction and responsive communication matter because the arrangement is part-time and remote; experience in government, policy research, investment analysis or supply chain intelligence is a plus. GOOD FIT IF: you want paid, low-hours, high-leverage research work alongside other projects rather than a full-time post. DEADLINE: none published; applications appear to be rolling.

item.title: Secure AI Futures Lab: Research Fellow (India, hybrid)
item.description:
Organisation: Secure AI Futures Lab (SAFL), a SteadRise project (formerly Impact Academy)

Location: India, at SAFL's Secure AI Hubs. Hybrid, with a remote-first first month.

Award: INR 100,000 to 400,000 per month, all-inclusive. Internship level: INR 50,000 to 100,000 per month. A senior version of the role is available for people with significant relevant experience. No application fee.

Duration: Full-time, fixed-term contract of 6 to 12 months

Deadline: Rolling / undated

SAFL, described as South Asia's first research and capacity-building lab for navigating powerful AI, is hiring more than one Research Fellow. Its foundational work is supported by Schmidt Sciences and the Future of Life Institute among others. THE ROLE: original research carried from an open question to a finished result. The lab wants people who can take a question nobody has answered, choose a method that fits it, do the work and write up a result others can check, working closely with the research leads and with room to shape their own agenda and the wider one. RESEARCH AREAS, two broad tracks; you need to be deep in one and able to speak to the others. Managing AI Risks: technical AI governance and policy (the frameworks advanced AI needs and the technical artifacts they depend on, covering evaluation standards, incident reporting, logging and provenance, attribution methods, liability and accountability, and turning technical evidence into standards Indian and international bodies can adopt), and AI security and alignment research (the safety and security of AI systems themselves, including AI and cybersecurity and the security of systems AI is deployed on top of, such as India's digital public infrastructure). Societal and Economic Impacts: the economic impacts of AI on labour, growth and public finances with attention to India and other developing economies, plus psycho-social effects. BAR: at least 3 years of hands-on research experience, described as the lab's most senior research bar, though exceptional people without that experience are encouraged to apply and junior/internship versions exist. HONEST WARNING FROM THE POSTING: 'The work is demanding, and we mean that plainly.' Priorities change as the field changes; output goes to funders, government bodies and outside researchers. Not a role with fixed scope or settled routine. RELATED OPENING: SAFL is also hiring a Scientific Communicator, plus an Organisation Operations Specialist, a Special Projects Fellow and a general expression of interest. DEADLINE: none published; rolling.

A science communication and information-design role at SAFL, South Asia's first research and capacity-building lab for navigating powerful AI, whose foundational work is supported by Schmidt Sciences and the Future of Life Institute among others. THE ROLE: turn the lab's research into clear writing and visuals for funders, partners, policymakers and the public. You read technical and policy work on AI and explain it in plain language without losing the substance. NOTE THAT A LARGE PART OF THIS ROLE IS VISUAL: building slide decks and visual maps that show what the lab works on and how the parts fit together, used for fundraising and partner updates. You work closely with the research and leadership team. WHAT THEY WANT: ideally 2 to 5 years of relevant experience, though the posting says a strong body of work can stand in for years. You do not need to be a known voice in the field; you do need to write clearly, learn their research quickly and care about getting it right. WHAT YOU WOULD BE EXPLAINING: technical AI governance and policy (evaluation standards, incident reporting, logging and provenance, attribution, liability), AI security and alignment research including the security of India's digital public infrastructure, and the societal and economic impacts of AI on labour, growth and public finances in India and other developing economies. You will often be the first person to put new research into words a non-expert can follow, priorities shift as the field shifts, and the work goes straight to funders, government partners and the public. Not a role with fixed scope or settled routine. DEADLINE: none published; rolling.

item.title: INHABIT #16 and #17: Artist-in-Residence 2027 (Max Planck Institute for Empirical Aesthetics)
item.description:
Organisation: Max Planck Institute for Empirical Aesthetics

Location: Frankfurt am Main, Germany

Award: Artist's fee of EUR 8,000 plus an accommodation fee of EUR 2,000, a production budget depending on the project, and travel costs to and within Frankfurt. Also included: realisation of the final project, collaborations with scientists, access to the institute's library, sound studio and scientific facilities, and curatorial support throughout the residency. No application fee.

Duration: Four months. Two slots: INHABIT #16 runs April to July 2027, INHABIT #17 runs September to December 2027

Deadline: 01 Sep 2026

INHABIT is the artist-in-residence programme of the Max Planck Institute for Empirical Aesthetics in Frankfurt am Main, which invites artists from various disciplines to collaborate with its scientists and researchers, treating artistic thinking and knowledge as reflective practices in their own right. The 2027 call is addressed to artists from the performing arts and music, who spend four months creating new work, or developing an existing project, inside a scientific research environment and in dialogue with the institute's researchers. Two slots are open for 2027: INHABIT #16 from April to July 2027 and INHABIT #17 from September to December 2027. Work developed during the residency is presented in cooperation with local arts institutions as an exhibition, performance, concert or other format, complemented by discursive formats. WHO THEY ARE LOOKING FOR: artists from the performing arts and music interested in interdisciplinary collaboration between artistic and scientific fields; artists open to developing and sharing a project as an exhibition, performance, concert or another format; and artists active in contemporary culture who respond to the institute with innovative and challenging ideas. WHAT IS OFFERED: an artist's fee of EUR 8,000, an accommodation fee of EUR 2,000, a project-dependent production budget, travel costs to and in Frankfurt, realisation of the final project, collaborations with scientists, access to the library, sound studio and scientific facilities, and curatorial support during the residency. APPLY through the institute's e-recruiting portal by 1 September 2026, 23:59 CET; the jury decision follows in November 2026. No fee.

item.title: Tartu UNESCO City of Literature Residency for Writers and Translators, Autumn 2026
item.description:
Organisation: Estonian Literary Society (Eesti Kirjanduse Selts), Focal Point for Tartu UNESCO City of Literature

Location: Tartu, Estonia. Open to writers, poets and translators of Estonian literature worldwide.

Award: Monthly stipend of EUR 600 for the two-month stay (EUR 1,200 in total), plus reimbursement of travel costs up to EUR 350. Free accommodation is provided in the Karl Ristikivi residency apartment, which has a bedroom, living room, kitchen, bathroom and exhibition room. One resident is selected. No application fee.

Duration: Two months, 15 October to 15 December 2026, with some flexibility on exact dates

Deadline: 01 Sep 2026

The Estonian Literary Society, which coordinates Tartu UNESCO City of Literature, runs an international residency programme for writers and translators that has hosted authors from Slovenia, Ireland, Hungary, the USA, the UK, Ukraine and Canada since 2017. This is the open call for the autumn 2026 slot: one resident stays two months in the Karl Ristikivi residency apartment in Tartu, working on their own writing or translation while connecting with the local literary scene. WHAT THE RESIDENCY OFFERS: a EUR 600 monthly stipend, travel reimbursement up to EUR 350, free accommodation, a local support coordinator to help arrange cultural engagements, and opportunities to perform and present at literary events. The autumn period covers the interdisciplinary literary festival Crazy Tartu on 12 to 14 November, and the resident is offered a slot to perform there alongside writers, poets, musicians and artists from Estonia and abroad. ELIGIBILITY: open to writers, poets and translators of Estonian literature of any nationality; applicants need an upper-intermediate level of spoken English, at least one published book, screenplay, theatre script or translation from Estonian into another language, a demonstrable interest in Estonian culture and literature, a willingness to take part in local literary activities, and a commitment to working on their own literary project during the stay. HOW TO APPLY: complete the online application form linked from the residency page and upload a fragment of up to five pages of a published text (in Estonian or English) or of a published translation. SELECTION: made by a committee representing the Estonian Literary Society, the Estonian Writers Union, the Estonian Literary Museum and the Tartu Literature House Foundation. Results are announced before 15 September 2026. The programme's stated aims are to enhance international exchange, diversify the local literary scene, introduce new foreign authors and their work to Estonian readers, and build lasting connections beyond the residency period. Questions: Marja Unt, eks@kirjandus.ee. Deadline 1 September 2026.

item.title: Le Garage Moderne: OASIS International Artist Residencies 2026 (Bordeaux)
item.description:
Organisation: Le Garage Moderne (European OASIS project)

Location: Bacalan district, Bordeaux, France. Le Garage Moderne is a non-profit car garage and bicycle workshop, a canteen serving sponsored meals, and a cultural venue housing 11 permanent artists, makers and craftswomen, recently returned to its 19th-century building after a two-and-a-half-year renovation.

Award: Five grants. Each artist receives a fee of EUR 1,300 gross (taxes may apply depending on legal status), up to EUR 600 for production expenses such as raw materials, technical services or special tools, a lump-sum travel grant scaled to distance with top-ups for green travel options, a per diem of EUR 45 per day, and accommodation in a self-catering hotel. Access to the shared tools and spaces of Le Garage Moderne is included, subject to the association's regulations. No application fee.

Duration: Two weeks on site. Five overlapping two-week slots, and applicants may choose one or more: 9 to 22 November, 16 to 29 November, 23 November to 6 December, 30 November to 13 December, and 7 to 20 December 2026. Deadline 1 September 2026; pre-selection interviews 15 September; final selection announced 1 October 2026.

Deadline: 01 Sep 2026

Second year of Le Garage Moderne's residency cycle within the European OASIS project, offering five grants to international artists for two-week stays in Bordeaux. THE SITE IS THE POINT. Le Garage Moderne is a working non-profit car and bicycle workshop with a neighbourhood canteen and a versatile venue for performing arts, concerts and community gatherings, all at once a productive space, a public space and a community-driven common. Having just moved back into its 19th-century building after a long renovation, the team describes machines and workbenches back in place and a brand-new playground, and invites residents to take over the space and explore its physical and social possibilities. They ask for SITE-SPECIFIC PROPOSALS that play with the verticality, the scale of the space, the community and what they call the hive-like vibe of the venue, where everyone runs around, shouts, gets their hands dirty and learns in the process. DISCIPLINES: any, explicitly including design, visual art, performing arts, film, small-scale architecture, emergency architecture, craft-making, street furniture, sound, and interdisciplinary or community-based practices. Proposals combining artistic creation with the spatial and the social are especially encouraged, and the organisers say plainly that they want to be surprised. WHAT IS EXPECTED: openness to exchange and collaboration with the 11 permanent residents and with 3 local artists recruited through a separate OASIS call; participation in 2 days of masterclass open to members and community, where you describe and share your practice, technique and working context with fellow OASIS residents, local artists, members and staff; and a public outcome, which need not be a large event but must be something the public can experience. RIGHTS: work produced during the residency remains the artist's property, but documentation of it is made by Le Garage Moderne and will be publicised by them for three years after the residency. Note this is a different OASIS partner call from the OASis In the Park (Naples) and Disappearing Landscape (High Tatras) rounds under the same European project.

item.title: AIXI Labs: Research Fellowship (rolling, quarterly rounds)
item.description:
Organisation: AIXI Labs

Location: Fully remote, open worldwide; fellows may also work from the organisation's London base in the United Kingdom.

Award: GBP 2,000 to GBP 3,500 per month stipend, plus a compute budget for machine-learning work. Free to apply.

Duration: Roughly one quarter (about 3 months) per fellowship. Quarterly rounds, rolling applications. Renewal possible in exceptional cases.

Deadline: Rolling / undated

AIXI Labs is a small London-based non-profit doing AI safety research grounded in algorithmic information theory. Its stated position is that most AI research today is either mathematically clean but narrow, or practical but too opaque for rigorous safety analysis; the lab targets a third category, methods general enough to describe powerful agents and provable enough to support real safety claims, using AIXI (the theoretical model of unbounded artificial superintelligence) and then porting the strongest of those ideas to modern LLM-based agents. The fellowship is a quarterly, rolling programme for researchers who want to work on this agenda under close mentorship from the core team: Cole Wyeth (Founder and Executive Director), Marcus Hutter (Research Director) and Aram Ebtekar (Founding Research Scientist). Fellows pursue a focused research project over roughly a quarter and receive a monthly stipend plus a compute budget for machine-learning work. The fellowship is fully remote, so fellows may work from anywhere in the world or from the London base. RESPONSIBILITIES: pursue a self-directed research project aligned with the lab's algorithmic-information-theoretic approach to AI safety, spanning anything from foundational theory to empirical tests with LLM-based agents; shape the project direction around your own strengths and interests, as the lab supports a range of work within this framework; and contribute papers, blog posts or other written output communicating results to the broader AI safety and ML research communities. MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS: a research background at the level of a current PhD student (for primarily empirical projects, a master's-level command of the relevant mathematics paired with substantial industry or applied research experience can also qualify); solid grounding in probability, statistics, information theory and reinforcement learning, sufficient to engage seriously with AIXI-style theoretical models (prior expertise in algorithmic information theory or AIXI is NOT required); strong verbal and written communication skills; genuine motivation to reduce existential risk from advanced AI and enthusiasm for the lab's kind of work. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS: publications at top ML, AI or theory venues such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ALT or COLT, though the lab values the strength of your best work over volume; background in algorithmic information theory, computability theory, learning theory or related theoretical computer science; experience fine-tuning, evaluating or red-teaming LLM-based and/or RL agents; prior engagement with the UAI/AIXI community or related fields, including members of the lab's online reading groups. APPLICATIONS are reviewed on a rolling basis and previous applicants remain eligible for later rounds.

item.title: Physical AI Safety Institute: Research Fellowship (expression of interest)
item.description:
Organisation: Physical AI Safety Institute (PAISI)

Location: Not stated in the call. PAISI is a US 501(c)(3) nonprofit and its team is affiliated with UC Berkeley and the Toyota Technological Institute at Chicago; because fellows are given access to physical robot platforms, expect an in-person or hybrid component. No nationality restriction is stated for expressions of interest.

Award: Stipend amount is not published. Fellows receive a stipend, access to physical robot platforms, compute for simulation and training, and structured mentorship. PAISI was seeded by a grant from BlueDot Impact. Free to submit an expression of interest.

Duration: 12 weeks per cohort. Target cohorts are Winter 2026, Spring 2027 and Summer 2027; the expression-of-interest form asks you to pick your preferred dates.

Deadline: Rolling / undated

Robot foundation models (pi-zero, OpenVLA, GR00T and others) are approaching widespread deployment on the back of more than USD 18 billion in funding, and almost nobody is working on their safety. The Physical AI Safety Institute, a new nonprofit founded by Bear Haon and Kaylene Stocking and seeded by a grant from BlueDot Impact, describes itself as a capacity-building organisation growing the community that develops techniques to interpret, align and control robot foundation models. Its research fellowship runs in 12-week cohorts: each fellow works within a stream led by a mentor on a concrete problem in physical AI safety, with mentors drawn from researchers with track records in robot foundation models, mechanistic interpretability, safe control or adversarial robustness for embodied systems. Each cohort ends with a research symposium where fellows present their work. STREAMS: mechanistic interpretability (sparse autoencoders and activation patching for VLA and WAM architectures); adversarial robustness (jailbreaking and prompt injection in the embodied action space); runtime monitoring (detecting when a policy operates outside its competence envelope); sim-to-real safety transfer (do safety behaviours survive deployment on physical hardware); and robot security (cyberattack vectors, data poisoning and supply chain for deployed robot models). WHO SHOULD APPLY: researchers with strong technical foundations in robotics or machine learning and a demonstrated interest in safety; prior safety experience is not required. PROCESS: this stage is an expression of interest, not a full application. The form takes about two minutes and asks you to pick your stream and preferred cohort dates; concrete details including stipend figures and application deadlines are shared through that channel, and neither is published on the site as of listing. PAISI also publishes seven free curriculum modules running from classical robot safety through VLA interpretability, adversarial robustness and runtime monitoring to deployment evaluation, plus a white paper, The Case for Physical AI Safety, at paisi.ai/the-case-for-physical-ai-safety. item.description:

Deadline: Closed 28 Aug 2026

The annual DARC PhD/Research Workshop, organised by the Digital Aesthetics Research Center at Aarhus University with transmediale, responds to transmediale's 2027 thematic framework. THEME: 'Interstices: Research (in) the gaps'. An interstice is the small space between objects set closely together, the cords in a rope or the atoms in a crystal lattice: an emptiness produced by the structure it belongs to, and without which that structure could not be what it is. In crystallography, interstitial sites are the spaces a lattice and its basis generate but do not fill, and interstitial diffusion, the movement of small atoms through the gaps of a host lattice, is the mechanism by which materials transform. The call asks what the equivalent sites are in social, cultural and computational structures: where are the gaps these combinations generate but do not fill, what moves through them, and do they carry transformative power? It works through Yancey Strickler's dark forest theory of the internet (the withdrawal of meaningful exchange from the open, surveilled, indexed web into private channels), the Dark Forest Collective's anthology and its 'cozyweb' of small sheltered spaces, dark nets, miniverses and moving castles as interstitial spaces produced by and defined against the dominant web, and Bogna Konior's extension of the dark forest metaphor to the opacity of AI systems, where silence is refusal rather than absence and the forest is increasingly inhabited by other-than-human intelligences that opt out of engagement with people. Where big tech pursues efficiency through the automation of human perception, cognition, identification and aesthetics, artists and researchers explore the non/more-than-human, glitchy, noisy, machinic, datafied and dark to build new expression and critique of data-ism and what is marketed as artificial intelligence, including the dangers and potentials inside badly curated data models, between polluting data centres, and in skeuomorphic interfaces. WHAT THEY WANT: proposals from artists, researchers and practitioners for work that occupies and moves through gaps that are social as well as structural, ontological and material. The gaps are physical too: the heat of data centres and their thirst for water, latency in the cables, unindexed nodes. The call invites speculations, practical interventions and inferences that fill the gaps and expand the diversity of possible communications and communities that can inhabit dark forests, including those built on, against and beneath the infrastructures underlying them, and welcomes work on the (dis-)continuous histories of technological exploration of computational infrastructures over the last 30 years or longer, and on how current artistic, theoretical and technical explorations repeat or break from them. WHO: PhD candidates and early-career researchers, with submissions welcome from researchers inside and outside the academy, including artists, designers and curators. PARTICIPANT EXPECTATIONS: participants write a paper and present it at the workshop, and on the basis of that peer review shorten the research into a newspaper-length article for distribution at the transmediale festival. The call is an invitation into the development process: selected artists get access to the technologies, datasets, interfaces and assumptions that shape these systems while they are still being built. Duration: Touring and implementation 1 March 2027 to 31 January 2028 (11 months).

Deadline: 22 Oct 2026

Perform Europe is the EU's dedicated cross-border touring scheme for the performing arts, run by a six-organisation consortium and co-funded by Creative Europe. It funds partnerships of at least three organisations from three different Creative Europe countries to tour a finished performing arts work in at least three countries, with an explicit emphasis on greener, more inclusive and more equitable touring practice. Eligible disciplines are circus, dance, outdoor arts, performance art, puppetry and theatre; LIVE MUSIC AND OPERA ARE EXCLUDED, and production costs for new creations are not covered since the work must already be finished before 1 March 2027. Applicants pick one of three grant tiers with no fixed criteria per tier, and may request up to EUR 5,000 in top-ups for accessibility and sustainability measures. Five percent of the total fund is ring-fenced for proposals involving Ukrainian partners or supporting the Ukrainian performing arts sector. All 41 Creative Europe countries are eligible, including Albania, Armenia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Iceland, Kosovo, Liechtenstein, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Norway, Serbia, Tunisia and Ukraine, but the UK is not. TIMING: applications close 22 October 2026 at 23:59 CEST, selected partnerships are announced in January 2027, and activity may only start from 1 March 2027. A Matchmaking Platform with over 2,300 registered professionals is available for finding partners before applying. CORE PRIORITY: each partnership must pick either diversity and inclusion or the fight against climate change as its core priority, and must also include measures addressing the other one; that choice has to run visibly through the whole application rather than sit in one section. WHO COUNTS AS A PARTNER: both organisations and individual professionals are eligible, so a partner can be an artist, collective, company, producer, presenter, venue, festival, residency, educational institution or NGO. Eligibility is decided by where you are legally based. The partnership appoints a lead partner who submits, signs and receives the grant. ELIGIBLE COSTS: artistic fees and salaries, travel, accommodation, subsistence, administration, reporting, communication, translation, surtitling, equipment transport, copyright fees, access and environmental measures, complementary activities and capacity building. Venue and equipment rental or purchase is capped at 5 percent of the requested grant, and preparation costs for presenting an existing work at 10 percent. PAYMENT: 60 percent after signing, 20 percent after the first narrative and financial report is approved, and the final 20 percent after completion and EU approval of Perform Europe's own final report. Top-ups are reimbursed only after the project ends and documentation is approved, so budget for the cash-flow gap. PRACTICAL: every partner must register for a Perform Europe account before submission and approval can take several working days, so do not leave that to the last week.

Outer Ear is Musikfonds' dedicated special programme for participatory projects in experimental music, and the strand that most cleanly matches an experimental and sound-art public-programme brief rather than concert-series funding. It emphasises the creative process and audience participation over finished works, explicitly targeting audiences for experimental music, which makes it suitable for workshop-plus-presentation formats, listening programmes and process-led sound art events. Application windows run twice yearly: 1 to 30 April 2026 (closed) and 1 to 30 October 2026, the next live deadline. THE FIRST OUTER EAR ROUND WAS HIGHLY COMPETITIVE, with 14 projects approved at an 8.6 percent success rate, so treat it as a long shot. As with all Musikfonds strands, the applicant must be based in Germany, projects abroad are ineligible, and double-funding with BKM or with projects run by permanently institutionally supported bodies is excluded. item.title: Rory Peck Trust: Crisis Fund for Freelance Journalists
item.description:
Organisation: Rory Peck Trust

Location: Remote (worldwide); London-based organisation supporting freelancers anywhere

Award: Individual emergency grants; amounts are set case by case from an assessment of circumstances and need. No application fee.

Duration: One-off emergency assistance; assessment takes roughly one to three weeks

Deadline: Rolling / undated

The Rory Peck Trust's Crisis Fund gives direct financial assistance to freelance news journalists whose work has put them in crisis: physical attack, urgent medical costs, replacement of confiscated or destroyed equipment, forced relocation, or support for the family of a journalist who has been injured, imprisoned, kidnapped or killed. This is one of the few funds built specifically for freelancers working in conflict and high-risk environments, who are usually outside any staff safety net. ELIGIBILITY: professional freelance journalists in news and current affairs whose sole income comes from journalism, who have been working freelance for at least the last 12 months and can provide reference letters from editors, who have no access to other financial or government support and no contractual benefits such as sick pay or social security. The crisis must have happened within the last six months and must be evidenced (invoices, bank statements). Anyone who received Rory Peck Trust support in the last three years is ineligible. The Trust also runs a separate Therapy Fund and a HEFAT safety-training fund. Applications are rolling, in English, French, Arabic, Spanish, Ukrainian or Russian. Contact assistance@rorypecktrust.org or info@rorypecktrust.org.
